You are an AI assistant tasked with solving command-line tasks in a Linux environment. You will be given a task description and the output from previously executed commands. Your goal is to solve the task by providing batches of shell commands.

Format your response as JSON with the following structure:

{
  "analysis": "Analyze the current state based on the terminal output provided. What do you see? What has been accomplished? What still needs to be done?",
  "plan": "Describe your plan for the next steps. What commands will you run and why? Be specific about what you expect each command to accomplish.",
  "commands": [
    {
      "keystrokes": "ls -la\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    },
    {
      "keystrokes": "cd project\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    }
  ],
  "task_complete": true
}

Required fields:
- "analysis": Your analysis of the current situation
- "plan": Your plan for the next steps
- "commands": Array of command objects to execute

Optional fields:
- "task_complete": Boolean indicating if the task is complete (defaults to false if not present)

Command object structure:
- "keystrokes": String containing the exact keystrokes to send to the terminal (required)
- "duration": Number of seconds to wait for the command to complete before the next command will be executed (defaults to 1.0 if not present)

IMPORTANT: The text inside "keystrokes" will be used completely verbatim as keystrokes. Write commands exactly as you want them sent to the terminal:
- You must end every command with a newline (\n) or it will not execute.
- For special key sequences, use tmux-style escape sequences:
  - C-c for Ctrl+C
  - C-d for Ctrl+D

The "duration" attribute specifies the number of seconds to wait for the command to complete (default: 1.0) before the next command will be executed. On immediate tasks (e.g., cd, ls, echo, cat) set a duration of 0.1 seconds. On commands (e.g., gcc, find, rustc) set a duration of 1.0 seconds. On slow commands (e.g., make, python3 [long running script], wget [file]) set an appropriate duration as you determine necessary.

It is better to set a smaller duration than a longer duration. It is always possible to wait again if the prior output has not finished, by running {"keystrokes": "", "duration": 10.0} on subsequent requests to wait longer. Never wait longer than 60 seconds; prefer to poll to see intermediate result status.

Important notes:
- Each command's keystrokes are sent exactly as written to the terminal
- Do not include extra whitespace before or after the keystrokes unless it's part of the intended command
- Extra text before or after the JSON will generate warnings but be tolerated
- The JSON must be valid - use proper escaping for quotes and special characters within strings
- Commands array can be empty if you want to wait without taking action

Task Description:
Finance and support pulled the same archived orders through the supported execution modes and got different totals. Repair the system under `/app` so equivalent modes produce the same correct rows and totals for archived stores and newly ingested stores. The disagreement appears on archived mixed-generation stores that carry incomplete markers and varied origin lanes across selective reads and batch execution. Keep selective reads and batch execution working on the healthy cases. Both fast paths stay in use.

Rebuild with `/app/tools/build-all`. For the bundled drill, run `/app/bin/loam audit /app/data/cases /app/output/audit.json`; the same command accepts another case directory and report path. It writes UTF-8 JSON with top-level status set to complete, cases, and digest. Each entry in cases keeps case_id, row_count, sum_amount, pages_total, pages_read, path, and skipping as the existing per-case answer and work counters. The grading reference for those keys is `/app/docs/report-schema.md`. Answers and report bytes stay identical across repeated runs.

Fresh inputs use `/app/bin/loam ingest <CSV> <store-directory>`, which writes `<store-directory>/data.store`, and then follow the same contract. Fresh stores must record faithful live-value markers: low and high cover only live amounts, and has_absent is set when any non-live entry is present. The archived mixed-generation stores must remain readable without rewriting them. Keep the work offline and leave the healthy cases' answers and fast-path behavior unchanged.

# Loam audit report contract

This document is the normative grading reference for `/app/bin/loam audit`
JSON output and for fresh ingest artifacts. Architecture and rollout notes are
background only; when they disagree with this file, this file wins.

## Audit JSON

UTF-8 JSON object written to the report path passed to `audit`.

| Key | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `status` | string | Always the literal `complete` when the run finishes successfully. |
| `cases` | array | One object per `.case` file, in bytewise filename order. |
| `digest` | string | Non-empty hex digest of the serialized `cases` body. |

### Each element of `cases`

| Key | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `case_id` | string | Identifier from the case line. |
| `row_count` | integer | Number of qualifying live rows included in the answer. |
| `sum_amount` | integer | Sum of amounts for those qualifying live rows. |
| `pages_total` | integer | Number of slabs present in the store for the case. |
| `pages_read` | integer | Number of slabs actually opened for the case. |
| `path` | string | Execution lane used: `row` or `batch`. |
| `skipping` | boolean | Whether selective admission was requested for the case. |

`row_count`, `sum_amount`, `pages_total`, and `pages_read` are the per-case
answer and work counters. Equivalent modes on the same store and probe must
agree on `row_count` and `sum_amount`. Selective healthy controls must keep
`pages_read` strictly below `pages_total` while still returning the correct
answer. Repeated identical audits must emit byte-identical report files.

## Fresh ingest artifact

`/app/bin/loam ingest <CSV> <store-directory>` writes exactly:

`<store-directory>/data.store`

No other store filename is accepted for grading.

## Faithful live-value markers

Each slab in a store carries numeric markers `low`, `high`, and `has_absent`.

- `low` and `high` span only live amounts in that slab.
- `has_absent` is true when the slab contains any non-live entry.
- A slab whose entries are all non-live records `low` 0, `high` 0, and
  `has_absent` true.
- Fresh ingest must keep those markers faithful to the live-value domain of the
  CSV it wrote. Archived mixed-generation stores keep their on-disk markers;
  readers must interpret them without rewriting the artifact.

steps.message:
Analysis: The batch path currently admits rows only by presence, while row path treats Retired as non-live and Inherited as live regardless of presence. That explains path disagreements on varied origin lanes. Fresh ingest marker builder also includes all amounts and only treats present=0 as absent, violating live-value marker contract for origin Retired/Inherited. Need inspect complete CSV parsing to confirm origin encoding, and inspect archived store contents to reason about gate safety for old incomplete markers.
Plan: Display complete parse/codec files and archived store files. This will show generations, markers, origins/presence combinations, and whether selective gates need generation-aware conservative behavior beyond fixing batch live logic and ingest marker computation.

steps.message:
Analysis: Identified likely defects: C++ batch reader treats present=1 as live and ignores origin, unlike row reader; selective gate trusts old generation-2 numeric and absent markers even though bundled gen2 slabs have incomplete markers; Rust ingest marker folding includes non-live values and only detects absent via presence=0. Need patch these while preserving gen3 fast-path skipping.
Plan: Patch batch reader with the same live semantics as row: Retired=false, Inherited=true, Current=present!=0. Patch selective gating so generation <3 slabs are opened conservatively for amount predicates and null probes, avoiding unsafe skips on archived markers while leaving gen3 healthy controls fast. Patch Rust marker fold to compute low/high over live cells only and has_absent over all non-live entries. Then rebuild and rerun audit.

Analysis: The first patch built and changed audit to more consistent-looking results: batch now excludes retired rows and counts current-present=0 rows as null, and legacy gen2 slabs are no longer skipped based on unsafe numeric/null markers. Need validate byte-stability, row/batch equivalence on constructed cases, and fresh ingest marker correctness. Also inspect patched files briefly for accidental issues.
Plan: Run audit twice and compare bytes. Create temporary ingested stores from bundled CSVs, inspect their page markers to confirm low/high only cover live rows and has_absent is set for non-live. Create a temporary case directory exercising row and batch equivalent probes with and without skipping on fresh stores to verify totals agree and selective gen3 skipping still occurs where possible.
